'''Raghavan Narasimhan''' (August 31, 1937&ndash;October 3, 2015) was an [[Indian people|Indian]] [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Chicago]] who worked  on [[real manifold|real]] and [[complex manifold]]s and who solved the [[Levi problem]] for complex manifolds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/article/2015/10/15/raghavan-narasimhan-analytically-deft-mathematician-1937-2015|title=Raghavan Narasimhan, analytically deft mathematician, 1937-2015|work=uchicago.edu}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
He attended Loyola College in Madras, where, like many other well-known Indian mathematicians, he was taught by the French Jesuit priest Racine, and received his doctorate in 1963 from K. Chandrasekharan in Bombay. In 1966 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at Princeton. Narasimhan was a professor at the [[University of Chicago]].
